  • At least 8 years working experience in accounting / financial services related environment
  • A minimum of 3 years people management experience
  • Strong hedge fund administration experience, including performance fee calculations, hot issue allocations, share class accounting, and allocation methodologies
  • Deep understanding of alternative investment products and accounting treatments, including derivatives, swaps, options, futures, and forwards.

jobs.descriptionText:
Who we are looking for
Fund Accountant Associate 2 will be responsible for supporting a range of operational and fund accounting activities for the client portfolio. The role requires a strong understanding of investment lifecycle events, operational controls and supporting documentation. The successful candidate will independently manage assigned responsibilities, investigate exceptions and work closely with internal teams and external stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate service delivery.
Why this role is important to us
The team you will be joining is part of Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS), a leading provider of fund accounting, fund administration and operational support services to alternative investment managers and institutional investors.
The team acts as a key coordination and control point across the alternative investment servicing lifecycle. The team connects client requirements with operational execution, helps ensure that investment, transaction, cash, valuation and reporting information is complete and accurate, and drives timely resolution of exceptions. The role is important in maintaining service quality, strengthening the control environment and supporting scalable, technology-enabled delivery across private equity, private credit, fund-of-funds and direct investment structures.
What you will be responsible for
Independently process investment lifecycle events, including capital calls, distributions, interest receipts, fee transactions, paydowns and other investment-related activities..
Review and maintain supporting documentation received from agents, administrators and counterparties.
Support cash processing and cash reconciliation activities by comparing transaction records against supporting documentation and internal systems.
Assist in setup and maintenance of investment attributes and operational records within relevant platforms.
Monitor and investigate basic exceptions, missing information and reconciliation breaks.
Escalate issues and outstanding items promptly to senior team members.
Support preparation of operational reports and client deliverables.
Maintain accurate audit trails and document management records.
Follow established procedures, risk controls and information-security requirements.
Participate in process improvement initiatives and support testing activities when required.
What we value
This position provides an opportunity to gain exposure to a broad range of alternative investment products and operational activities, including private equity, private credit, fund-of-funds and other complex investment structures. The successful candidate will develop expertise in investment operations, cash management, documentation review and client servicing activities within a global operating environment.
We Value
Strong attention to detail
Ownership and accountability
Problem-solving mindset
Effective communication
Ability to work under pressure
Teamwork and collaboration
Continuous improvement mindset
Education And Preferred Qualifications
Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business or related discipline.
Approx 2 years related experience of relevant experience within fund accounting, fund administration, financial services or alternative investment operations.
Understanding of alternative investment structures and investment lifecycle events preferred.
Strong analytical and numerical skills.
Good Microsoft Excel skills.
Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong organisational and time-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to identify issues, investigate exceptions and escalate appropriately.
Role scope and working relationships
The Associate 2 role is critical in ensuring the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of operational processing while supporting a strong control environment and high-quality client service. The role works closely with middle-office and transaction-processing teams, document management, reconciliation, valuation, financial reporting, audit, technology, product and project-management partners. Responsibilities may vary by client, investment type and target operating model.

jobs.title: Financial Reporting, Associate 2
jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For
Responsible for the end-to-end preparation, analysis, and delivery of periodic (quarterly, semi-annual, annual and ad hoc) financial statements and related disclosures in accordance with IFRS, US GAAP, regulatory requirements, and client-specific reporting standards for alternative investment funds and registered funds, including Hedge, Private Equity, Fund-of-Funds, and other investment structures.
Why This Role Is Important To Us
The team you will be joining is part of State Street Global Delivery (SSGD). SSGD gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGD’s tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.
Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
What You Will Be Responsible For
As
Financial Reporting, Associate 2,
you will:
Set up and maintain reporting folders within shared drives and related reporting platforms for each fund throughout the reporting cycle, ensuring all supporting documentation for financial statement disclosures is obtained, validated, and properly organized. Research and resolve outstanding issues as required, and maintain accurate, complete, and well-structured records to support reporting, review, and audit requirements.
Prepare periodic financial statements:
Perform planning and readiness assessments prior to each reporting cycle to identify potential issuesand collaborate with applicable parties to resolve.
Conduct detailed reviews of general ledger balances, identify exceptions or discrepancies, and drive issue resolution with internal applicable parties.
Analyze and validate financial statement balances and disclosures to ensure accuracy, completeness, and overall reasonableness.
Draft financial statements disclosures in compliance with applicable accounting standards, including IFRS and US GAAP requirements.
Adhere to established financial reporting procedures, complete all required task lists, and obtain appropriate sign-offs in accordance with internal policies.
Identify opportunities for process improvement and recommend or implement technical initiatives to reporting procedures, controls, and workflows.
Ensure adherence to the financial statements production calendar.
Coordinate distribution of financial statements:
Assemble financial statements draft, all supporting documentation and calculations.
Managing the receipt of comments on financial statements drafts from external (and internal) parties. Ensure the timely research, resolution, and processing of comments.
Participating in the testing and implementation of financial reporting systems, platforms and templates, while identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, controls, and automation.
What We Value
These skills will help you succeed in this role
Strong critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to identify issues, evaluate risks, and deliver effective solutions in a fast-paced environment.
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline.
1+ years of financial services relevant working experience.
Progress toward, or possession of, a recognized professional accounting qualification (e.g., CFA, CPA, ACCA, CA) is an asset.
Knowledge of preparation of financial statements (IFRS and US GAAP) is an asset.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, with advanced skills in Excel, including complex formulas, data validation, pivot tables, and financial reporting tools.
Effective English listening and written communication skills.
Superior attention to detail, time management, and organizational skills.
Ability to effectively manage multi-tasks, work under pressure, meet tight deadlines, and deliver high-quality results.
Additional Requirements
Overtime may be required
Ability to work across time zones when required
Flexibility during peak reporting periods

jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For
The Senior Associate - AM will be responsible for performing and reviewing key fund accounting activities, including investment activity processing, reconciliations and NAV package preparation. The role focuses on delivering accurate and timely accounting outputs, resolving day-to-day issues and supporting a strong control environment.
Why This Role Is Important To Us
The team you will be joining is part of Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS), a recognized provider of fund accounting and administration services to alternative investment clients. Our team provides end-to-end support for North American clients, with a focus on private equity, Fund of Fund and other complex investment structures. Our team supports key fund operations, including investment activity processing, valuation, NAV package production, and audit-related activities.
Join us if making your mark in the alternative investment industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
What You Will Be Responsible For
As Senior Associate - AM you will:
Process and review investment activity to ensure transactions are accurately recorded in accordance with the playbook and client requirements.
Prepare and review reconciliations, NAV packages and supporting schedules to ensure completeness, accuracy and timely delivery.
Investigate and resolve accounting discrepancies, reconciliation breaks and routine operational issues.
Support client ad hoc requests and coordinate with relevant stakeholders on assigned accounting and operational matters.
Execute key controls effectively and escalate identified issues and potential risks in a timely manner.
Demonstrate ownership of assigned funds, deliverables and related processes.
Participate in system testing, automation initiatives and process improvement activities when assigned.
Support junior team members by sharing process knowledge and providing day-to-day guidance when required.
What We Value
Good knowledge of private equity and Fund of Fund accounting.
Understanding of key alternative investment fund administration processes.
Strong attention to detail with analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines.
Effective communication and collaboration skills.
Ownership mindset with a willingness to learn and contribute to continuous improvement.
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or above in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; an accounting background is preferred.
2-4 years of experience in financial services, fund accounting and/or a back-office operations environment; experience in an accounting firm or fund house is preferred.
Working knowledge of private equity, Fund of Fund, and alternative investment products.
Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office skills.
Experience supporting audit requests and financial statement preparation is preferred.
Good written and verbal communication skills.
Professional qualifications such as CPA, ACCA or CFA are a plus.

jobs.title: Alpha Operations Portfolio Management, Senior Associate
jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For
The Alpha Portfolio Services team is a dedicated global business team working with Clients, SSC IT, client service, and the business operations teams to ensure accurate end-to-end oversight of Information Delivery to our clients. The Alpha Portfolio Services team is responsible for ensuring the Investment book of records is accurately maintained and ensuring accurate client portfolios are reflected on State Street platforms. The role will interact with the Clients (predominantly Front Office) and being a key liaison with various portfolio managers and internal SSC parties in identifying an issue as well as managing that a suitable resolution is found and communicated to the Client. The role will need to initiate and develop good communication and interpersonal relationship with business operations teams and IT and to maintain the high level of service that is currently being provided to all the clients.
Why this role is important to us
The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Global Services (SSGS). SSGS gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping, to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGS’ tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.
Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
What You Will Be Responsible For
As Middle Office, Senior Associate, you will
Ensure client queries relating to the Recordkeeping system and client file deliveries are tracked, with proactive management to ensure timely response and resolution
Perform daily checks on file deliverables to the clients, investigate and report discrepancies and ensure daily resolution of identified queries
Provide Subject Matter expertise for complex system architecture queries/changes
Perform an overview function for the Shared Services functions identifying operational trends, issues and areas for improvement.
Perform work independently within scope of established guidelines and according to specific procedures.
Investigate and resolve operational and various IT issues (e.g. Asset servicing, Trade Operations, Client Reporting)
Support and provide analysis for Client Change Request items impacting the Enterprise processes and Operating Models
Work independently to research and resolve problems considering multiple avenues for resolution. Trouble shoot issues and provide resolutions to various impacted teams
Communicate effectively on issues / problems to the Client and to SSC management and ensure a proper and timely follow-up to ensure resolution.
Provide guidance, support, act as resource and assist team members from multiple operational areas relating to Enterprise queries
Complete any ad-hoc tasks as identified by the line manager
What We Value
These skills will help you succeed in this role
Portfolio Valuations reconciliations/Investigations experience is required. Candidates should be able to validate portfolio movements day over day and highlight any issues.
Excellent technical ability, Excellent analytical skills are essential for this role.
Strong communication (especially written) and presentation skills to audiences of different sizes and levels of seniority.
Must be self-motivated, adaptable and show initiative in different circumstances and under pressure
Extensive asset management experience, including investment operations
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Degree in finance, business, technology or equivalent or relevant industry experience of 3-5 years
Experience in writing SQL, Oracle, Sybase is a plus
Strong MS Excel, Access, Word, Powerpoint skills necessary

jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For
Responsible for preparing, reviewing, analyzing, and delivering end-to-end financial reporting services for clients across APAC, EMEA, and North America in accordance with established procedures. The role requires close collaboration with global stakeholders and a strong focus on accuracy, quality, risk management, and timely delivery. The ideal candidate will bring strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills, while contributing to process improvement, operational excellence, and the continued enhancement of reporting controls and documentation.
Why This Role Is Important To Us
The team you will be joining is part of State Street Global Delivery (SSGD). SSGD gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGD’s tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.
Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
This role offers exposure to global financial reporting processes, cross-regional stakeholder management, and continuous improvement initiatives within a highly controlled financial services environment.
What You Will Be Responsible For
As
Financial Reporting, Senior Associate,
you will:
Prepare and review periodic and ad hoc financial statements, disclosures, and related reporting deliverables in accordance with applicable accounting standards and client requirements.
Coordinate and manage reporting deliverables, timelines, and stakeholder expectations to ensure accurate, timely, and high-quality completion of client reporting obligations.
Serve as a subject matter expert for financial reporting systems and processes by maintaining data integrity, resolving process queries, and providing guidance, support, and coaching to team members.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders across global locations to facilitate issue resolution, obtain required information, and support successful delivery of reporting requirements.
Maintain a strong risk and control environment by monitoring compliance with procedures, identifying operational risks, and escalating and resolving issues in a timely manner.
Review and enhance reporting processes, documentation, SOPs, process flows, and control frameworks to improve efficiency, consistency, quality, and operational effectiveness.
Support business initiatives and organizational objectives through process improvement, change management activities, knowledge sharing, and continuous development of team capabilities.
What We Value
These skills will help you succeed in this role
Strong critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to analyze complex issues, assess risks and impacts, identify root causes, and deliver practical solutions to operational and client challenges in a dynamic environment.
Effective collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with internal teams, clients, auditors, and global stakeholders.
A proactive ownership mindset, with a commitment to continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and delivering high-quality outcomes in a controlled environment.
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline.
3+ years of relevant working experience in financial services, fund administration, financial reporting, audit, or accounting.
Postgraduate qualifications or professional certifications such as CFA, CPA, ACCA, or CA, either completed or in progress, are preferred. Relevant experience in a Big 4 or reputable mid-tier accounting firm is also preferred.
Solid technical knowledge and practical experience in statutory reporting with a strong understanding of IFRS and GAAP requirements and their application.
Good understanding of managed investment funds, financial services, investment products, and applicable accounting standards.
Strong analytical mindset and attention to detail, with proven ability to identify issues, develop solutions, and support informed decision-making.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, with advanced Excel skills including complex formulas, data validation, pivot tables, and financial reporting tools.
Strong English written and verbal communication skills.
Proven ability to effectively manage multiple priorities, perform under pressure, meet tight deadlines, and consistently deliver high-quality results.
Additional Requirements
Overtime may be required during peak reporting periods.
Ability to work across time zones when required to support global stakeholders and reporting deadlines.

Who We Are Looking For
Associate 2 Fund Administrator will be responsible for independently processing investment activity on custody and/or accounting entries, preparing accurate and timely reconciliations integral to the completion of the Net Asset Value (NAV) that is used for alternative investment funds, Investor dealing and external publication, plus various other client specific reports distributed on a regular basis. This involves adherence to strict deadlines while maintaining close attention to detail, meanwhile involves investigating routine operational issues, and providing support to junior team members.
Why Is This Role Important To Us
The team you will be joining is part of Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS), recognized provider of fund accounting and/or administration services to Alternative Investment Asset Owner clients globally. Our Asset Owner Clients entrust us with the critical responsibility of managing the operational backbone that supports their investment portfolios. This role is central to ensuring the accuracy, timeliness, and transparency of key services—such as document management, cash processing, valuation, and performance reporting—that directly impact client confidence and investment decision-making.
What You Will Be Responsible For
As Fund Administrator Associate 2 you will:
Performance daily workflow independently and timely
Assisting with the accurate and timely production of the Net Asset Value
Verifying and ensuring all events have been processed accurately
Processing and reviewing various funds and/or investments’ activity on custodian & accounting
Supervising investigation and resolution of all reconciling cash and position items
Coordinating with other departments on miscellaneous fund queries and reconciliations
Assist in the preparation of operational activities related to document management, cash processing, valuation reconciliation, investment set up and performance reporting to support the delivery of accurate and timely services to asset owner clients.
Demonstrate working ability on MS office apps including Excel etc.
Assisting with training and development of staff
Execute key controls and promptly escalate identified issues
Participate in system testing, automation, and process improvement activities when assigned
What We Value
This position offers the successful candidate the opportunity to broaden their knowledge of private equity, private credit, and other alternative investments operating in a dynamic, deadline sensitive environment. The candidate will contribute to the development of the team, job staff training, liaising with external parties and enhancing client satisfaction.
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Degree in Business, Accounting or related field.
Approx 2 years’ related experience in a fund accounting environment, including knowledge of cash and position reconciliation in funds
Knowledge of unlisted products such as Private equity, real estate, etc.
Knowledge of custody cash payment/ receipt will be an advantage
Excellent attention to detail
Strong numerical / analytical skills
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
Highly computer literate
Excellent communication skills
Organized and Deadline-driven
Good team player, with supervisory experience a distinct advantage
Assist in the preparation of operational activities related to document management, cash processing, valuation reconciliation, and performance reporting to support the delivery of accurate and timely services to asset owner clients.

jobs.descriptionText:
Who we are looking for
We are looking for an entry-level professional responsible for supporting day-to-day operation activities in the team for complex alternative investment portfolios. The role focuses on accurate execution of operational processes, timely completion of assigned tasks, and adherence to established procedures and controls. The successful candidate will take ownership of service delivery, controls, issue resolution and people development in a fast-paced environment with multiple deadlines and evolving operating models.
Why this role is important to us
The team you will be joining is part of Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS), a leading provider of fund accounting, fund administration and operational support services to alternative investment managers and institutional investors.
The team acts as a key coordination and control point across the alternative investment servicing lifecycle. The team connects client requirements with operational execution, helps ensure that investment, transaction, cash, valuation and reporting information is complete and accurate, and drives timely resolution of exceptions. The role is important in maintaining service quality, strengthening the control environment and supporting scalable, technology-enabled delivery across private equity, private credit, fund-of-funds and direct investment structures.
What you will be responsible for
Assist in processing investment lifecycle events, including capital calls, distributions, interest receipts, fee payments and other client-related transactions.
Review and maintain supporting documentation received from agents, administrators and counterparties.
Support cash processing and cash reconciliation activities by comparing transaction records against supporting documentation and internal systems.
Assist in setup and maintenance of investment attributes and operational records within relevant platforms.
Monitor and investigate basic exceptions, missing information and reconciliation breaks.
Escalate issues and outstanding items promptly to senior team members.
Support preparation of operational reports and client deliverables.
Maintain accurate audit trails and document management records.
Follow established procedures, risk controls and information-security requirements.
Participate in process improvement initiatives and support testing activities when required.
What we value
This position provides an opportunity to gain exposure to a broad range of alternative investment products and operational activities, including private equity, private credit, fund-of-funds and other complex investment structures. The successful candidate will develop expertise in investment operations, cash management, documentation review and client servicing activities within a global operating environment.
We Value
Strong attention to detail
Ownership and accountability
Problem-solving mindset
Effective communication
Ability to work under pressure
Teamwork and collaboration
Continuous improvement mindset
Education And Preferred Qualifications
Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business or related discipline.
6 months to 1 year of relevant experience within fund accounting, fund administration, financial services or alternative investment operations.
Strong analytical and numerical skills.
Good Microsoft Excel skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong organisational and time-management skills.
Knowledge of alternative investment products is advantageous but not required.
Role scope and working relationships
The role works closely with middle-office and transaction-processing teams, document management, reconciliation, valuation, financial reporting, audit, technology, product and project-management partners. Responsibilities may vary by client, investment type and target operating model.

jobs.title: Alternative Ops Fund Accounting, Senior Associate
jobs.descriptionText:
Who we are looking for
Fund Accountant Senior Associate will serve as a subject matter expert and primary reviewer within the team. The role is responsible for overseeing complex operational activities, ensuring quality and control standards are consistently met, and supporting day-to-day delivery across assigned portfolios. The successful candidate will possess strong technical knowledge, sound judgement, and the ability to guide junior team members while maintaining excellent stakeholder relationships.
Why this role is important to us
The team you will be joining is part of Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS), a leading provider of fund accounting, fund administration and operational support services to alternative investment managers and institutional investors.
The team acts as a key coordination and control point across the alternative investment servicing lifecycle. The team connects client requirements with operational execution, helps ensure that investment, transaction, cash, valuation and reporting information is complete and accurate, and drives timely resolution of exceptions. The role is important in maintaining service quality, strengthening the control environment and supporting scalable, technology-enabled delivery across private equity, private credit, fund-of-funds and direct investment structures.
What you will be responsible for
Review operational processing completed by Associates and ensure outputs are accurate, complete and compliant with established procedures.
Review investment lifecycle transactions, including capital calls, distributions, interest receipts, fees, paydowns and related activities.
Validate market values and valuation inputs against supporting documentation, investigate significant movements or discrepancies, and ensure exceptions are appropriately documented, escalated and resolved.
Validate supporting documentation and ensure appropriate evidence is maintained.
Perform detailed investigation and review of complex reconciliation breaks and exceptions.
Execute reviewer controls and ensure maker-checker requirements are properly performed.
Identify control weaknesses, operational risks and procedural gaps.
Participate in issue investigations, root cause analysis and remediation activities.
Support operational incident reporting and corrective action tracking.
Act as a key contact for day-to-day operational matters and escalations.
Coordinate with custodians, counterparties, administrators and internal support teams to resolve outstanding items.
Communicate operational updates and risks to management on a timely basis.
Act as a key contact for day-to-day operational matters and escalations.
Coordinate with custodians, counterparties, administrators and internal support teams to resolve outstanding items.
Communicate operational updates and risks to management on a timely basis.
Provide technical guidance and coaching to Associates.
Support onboarding and training of new team members.
Share best practices and contribute to knowledge management initiatives.
Assist management with workload coordination and delivery monitoring.
What we value
This position provides an opportunity to gain exposure to a broad range of alternative investment products and operational activities, including private equity, private credit, fund-of-funds and other complex investment structures. The successful candidate will develop expertise in investment operations, cash management, documentation review and client servicing activities within a global operating environment.
We Value
Strong technical and operational expertise.
Excellent quality and risk awareness.
Sound judgement and decision-making skills.
Proactive issue identification and resolution.
Strong stakeholder management capabilities.
Ability to coach and develop junior staff.
Ownership, accountability and professionalism.
Education And Preferred Qualifications
Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business or related discipline.
4-6 years related experience of relevant experience within fund accounting, fund administration, financial services or alternative investment operations.
Understanding of alternative investment structures and investment lifecycle events preferred.
Advanced Excel and data analysis skills.
Prior reviewer or checking experience preferred.
Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong organisational and time-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to identify issues, investigate exceptions and escalate appropriately.
Role scope and working relationships
The role is critical in ensuring the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of operational processing and reviewing while supporting a strong control environment and high-quality client service. The role works closely with middle-office and transaction-processing teams, document management, reconciliation, valuation, financial reporting, audit, technology, product and project-management partners. Responsibilities may vary by client, investment type and target operating model.

  • Execute reviewer controls and ensure maker-checker requirements are properly performed.

  • Act as a key contact for day-to-day operational matters and escalations.

jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For:
This role will serve business operations from risk governance, service governance and project management perspective. Such as leading and driving multiple governance committees, aiming to better support business from different angles (risk, training, Talent, etc.) as well as support our head of operation to drive corporate strategy and implementation.
This role requires a broader view when collaborating with various functional teams across the entity. Independent analytics and testing on an existing process and always open minded for constructive feedbacks and suggestions.
Why This Role Is Important To Us:
The team you will be joining is in the Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS) department which is a part of State Street. AIS is a recognized industry-leading provider of fund accounting, fund administration and risk services to hedge funds and private equity funds. These services are fully integrated to provide complete end-to-end solutions that span the front-, middle- and back-office requirements of institutional investors.
What You Will Be Responsible For:
Internal operations and staff Management
Supervise employees on a daily basis, including tasks delegation, employee development, goal setting, performance appraisal, etc.
Review accounting, financial statements, correspondence and deliverables of employees.
Coordinate with auditors internal and external to meet deadlines and requirements.
Ensure all internal controls and compliance procedures are properly implemented
Client relationship management
Close interaction with a portfolio of clients on a regular basis
To pro-actively identify/ensure understanding of client’s needs and to coordinate internally to support the client’s requirements/resolve client issues
Manage the process of new business/clients onboarding to State Street.
Projects:
Participate in special client or internal projects as required
Academy And Experience Required:
The AVP interacts with all levels of professionals both internally and externally. A strong foundation with communication and interpersonal skills are essential. Candidates must also have the following attributes, skills and experience:
Proactive and multi –task
Strong Client Relationship Experience Preferred
Prior staff management experience
Qualified Accountant; strong accounting and/or fund administration experience
Working experience in audit/private equity industry/fund administration sectors is preferred
Proficiency in Chinese. English is a must
8 years+ relevant working experience is required
About State Street
What we do.
State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.
Work, Live and Grow.
We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary in locations, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans among other perks. You’ll have access to flexible Work Program to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.
Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility.
We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspective are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. We warmly welcome the candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. You will have tools to help balance your professional and personal life, paid volunteer days, matching gift program and access to employee networks that help you stay connected to what matters to you.
State Street is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer.

jobs.title: Alternative Ops Fund Accounting, Senior Associate
jobs.descriptionText:
About The Private Markets Fund Of Funds Team
The Private Markets Fund of Funds (FoF) team supports the accounting and administration of investment structures that invest across underlying private market funds and, where applicable, co-investments. The team supports a broad range of private market strategies and structures, delivering accurate accounting records, Net Asset Value (NAV) production, investor reporting, and other client-specific deliverables. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the processing and reporting of capital calls, distributions, cash transactions, management fees, carried interest, expenses, reconciliations, and NAV-related activities. Team members work within established client requirements, operating procedures, and control frameworks to maintain complete and accurate accounting records and support timely reporting.
Who We Are Looking For
The Senior Associate (AM), Private Markets Fund of Funds Fund Accountant is responsible for coordinating day-to-day accounting and administration activities for assigned clients and investment structures. The role provides technical and process oversight, reviews NAV and reporting deliverables, resolves complex operational issues, supports projects and migrations, and provides guidance and on-the-job training to junior colleagues. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong ownership, sound judgment, effective stakeholder communication, and a consistent focus on quality, controls, and timely delivery.
Why This Role Is Important to Us
The team you will join is part of Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS), a recognized industry-leading provider of fund accounting, fund administration, and risk services to private equity, private credit, real estate, hedge fund, and other alternative investment clients. Our services are fully integrated to provide comprehensive end-to-end solutions across front-, middle-, and back-office operations.
Join us if you are ready to apply strong technical knowledge, coordinate complex fund accounting deliverables, and help strengthen team capability and client service.
What You Will Be Responsible For
Coordinate day-to-day accounting and administration activities for assigned Private Markets FoF clients and related investment structures, serving as a process subject matter resource.
Review NAV-related processes and deliverables, including bookkeeping, bank reconciliations, schedules of investments, partners’ capital statements, capital call and distribution allocations, management fee calculations, IRR and waterfall calculations, and relevant client-service deliverables.
Validate the completeness, accuracy, and timeliness of assigned deliverables and ensure that review comments and outstanding items are resolved appropriately.
Investigate and resolve complex accounting, reconciliation, and operational issues; document conclusions and escalate material risks or judgmental matters when required.
Communicate effectively with upstream teams, downstream teams, home-site colleagues, and other service partners to coordinate information, resolve issues, and meet delivery requirements.
Maintain procedures and control documentation and support adherence to corporate compliance requirements, risk policies, and standard operating procedures.
Identify opportunities to improve the daily operating model, controls, efficiency, and service quality, and support implementation with the manager.
Take an active role in projects, migrations, process enhancements, and other business initiatives, including planning and coordination of assigned workstreams.
Coordinate on-the-job training, provide technical and procedural guidance to junior colleagues, and contribute observations to staff development and succession-planning discussions.
Promote accountability, operational excellence, collaboration, knowledge sharing, and client focus across the team.
What We Value
Strong technical knowledge of private markets fund accounting and NAV production.
Ownership, sound judgment, and accountability for assigned deliverables and issue resolution.
Ability to review complex work, identify risks, and provide clear and constructive feedback.
Effective communication and collaboration across teams and locations.
Commitment to controls, continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and high-quality client service.
Key Skills
Advanced fund accounting, reconciliation, NAV, and financial-statement review skills.
Knowledge of capital activity, management fees, carried interest, IRR, waterfall calculations, and partnership accounting concepts.
Ability to analyze complex issues, determine practical next steps, and escalate appropriately.
Strong stakeholder communication, coordination, and follow-through.
Ability to maintain procedures, assess process risks, and contribute to control and operating-model enhancements.
Coaching and on-the-job training capability for junior team members.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills; experience with any private market fund accounting platform is an advantage.
Strong organization and prioritization in a deadline-driven environment.
Education And Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or above in accounting, finance, economics, or a related field; an accounting background is preferred.
A minimum of three years of experience in financial services, fund accounting, back-office operations, or a related field is preferred.
Relevant experience in private markets, private equity, fund-of-funds structures, or alternative investments is preferred.
Effective written and verbal English communication skills.
Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
Ability to prioritize under pressure, meet deadlines, and find practical solutions to complex, time-critical issues.

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. Strong ownership and accountability, with a client-service mindset and a consistent focus on quality and risk management.

Excellent organisation and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple deliverables, changing priorities and time-sensitive escalations.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with close attention to detail and the ability to distinguish small but significant differences in documents, data and transaction terms.
Clear, confident written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical or operational matters to clients, senior management and cross-functional partners.

Curiosity and a continuous-improvement mindset, with the confidence to challenge inefficient practices and propose practical, controlled solutions.
A professional, collaborative and resilient approach when working under pressure.

University degree in accounting, finance, economics, business, mathematics or a related discipline. A professional accounting or investment qualification, or progress towards one, is an advantage.

Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work effectively across locations, cultures and time zones.

The role works closely with client representatives, fund accounting and NAV teams, middle-office and transaction-processing teams, document management, reconciliation, valuation, financial reporting, audit, technology, product and project-management partners. jobs.title: Client Implementation & Service - Account Services Team, Officer
jobs.descriptionText:
About Us
Middle Office Account Services Team (also known as Transitions Team) is a Global Middle Office Team, which oversee and track Client’s events such as Account Launches, Account Terminations, Custody Changes, Custody Conversion, etc. with other internal State Street Teams. In addition, Account Services provides a centralized First Point of Contact (FPOC/primary contact) between the Client (and other interest parties) and internal State Street teams.
Purpose of Role
The position will support and maintain the Middle Office production processing of multiple client’s portfolio static data, and the coordination of Transition events such as New Account Setups, Account Restructures, Terminations, Account Maintenance and other changes.
The position requires regular independent interaction with internal teams, client contacts, custodians and other interest parties. The data elements gathered need to be maintained in an accurate and timely manner to help support the clients’ trading activities in addition to supporting numerous departments within the organization. The position will also be the primary point of contact internally and externally regarding the data elements, hence excellent interpersonal, communication and organizational skills are a must for the role.
Responsibilities And Duties
Complete the day-to-day responsibilities of the team within a strong risk and control environment that minimizes incidents and errors. Own the research and resolution of issues involving all operational and various IT areas (e.g. Asset Servicing, Trade Operations, Account Transitions, COACS). Conduct high-level analysis in specific areas of expertise, identify and resolve work-processing issues and make suggestions to streamline operations. Coordinate with Account Service management team to approve documented workflow, procedures and controls, determining impact of activity to other areas. Make proactive recommendations and solutions for problems resolution. Interface with senior level, internal and external stakeholders and other departments on complex matters and inquiries.
Liaise with colleagues within the Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, Japan, USA, UK and India State Street offices and divisions globally where required for query resolution. Support and provide analysis for Client Change Request items impacting the Enterprise processes and Operating Models.
Required Experience & Skills
Broad and in-depth understanding of the asset management industry, gained through working with an asset manager, portfolio manager or custodian
Broad and in-depth understanding of standards, methodologies, processes, systems and technology necessary to support investment management operations
Experience with writing and reviewing business specifications, procedures, operating models, etc.
Excellent analytical skills and ability to analyze quickly
Strong written and communication skills to people at all levels
Must be self-motivated, adaptable and show initiative in different circumstances and under pressure
Ability to work well in a team
Flexibility in working outside of your responsibilities and areas of expertise
Flexible working hours may be required
Bachelor’s degree with emphasis in finance, accounting, or technology or equivalent work experience in finance or accounting

Who We Are Looking For
We are seeking to recruit an enthusiastic Hedge Fund Accounting professional to join our team. The role is responsible for assisting the Officer/AVP in delivering end-to-end fund administration services, coaching and supporting A1/A2 members, providing on the job training, and acting as the main point of contact for internal teams and external clients and auditors.
The candidate will gain exposure to many client relationship management aspects with an excellent opportunity to gain experience in a fast moving financial services environment.
Why This Role Is Important To Us
The team you will be joining is part of
Alternative Investment Solutions (AIS)
, a recognized industry leader in providing fund accounting, fund administration, and risk services to hedge funds, private markets, and other alternative investment vehicles. AIS delivers fully integrated solutions across the investment lifecycle, providing clients with comprehensive front-, middle-, and back-office support to meet the evolving needs of institutional investors.
Join us if making your mark in the alternative investment industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
What You Will Be Responsible For
As Hedge Fund Accounting Senior Associate you will be responsible for
Net Asset Value Operations
Coordinating workflow and completing detailed preparation/review of Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Quarterly NAV pack, which includes:
Review cash and position reconciliations, validate portfolio pricing
Income and expense accrual
Partner/shareholder allocation calculations
Analysis of fund returns and performance in line with current market trends and projections
Other ad hoc reports as needed
Keeping abreast of new accounting standards and ensuing compliance on all accounts within the team
Implementing on the job training initiatives and ensuring consistent coaching and mentoring of staff.
Evaluate staffing needs while continually striving for greater efficiencies.
Ensure all controls and procedures are adhered to as well as make improvements where necessary.
Assisting the process of client migration, new business/clients onboarding.
Participate in other special projects or tasks where required.
Client Relationship Management
Develop and maintain a strong relationship with Investment Managers, brokers, auditors and all other fund participants by tackling queries, delivering NAV related reports.
Pro-actively identify/ensure understanding of client’s needs and coordinate internally to support the client’s requirements.
Provide solutions and/or to coordinate support to resolve client issues.
What We Value
These skills will help you succeed in this role
Good verbal and written English communication skills are required including report writing skills.
Good interpersonal skills and ability to communicate effectively at all levels within the organization
Good knowledge of hedge fund accounting, including NAV calculations, fund structures, investment products, and related operational processes
Strong organizational and time management skills – ability to prioritise tasks and perform effectively within strict deadlines.
Proficient in the use of MS Office tools in particular MS Excel.
Confident in dealing with difficult situations and be able to create innovative solutions to problems without a high degree of supervision.
Shows a growth mindset by adopting AI and digital tools to enhance ways of working, improve effectiveness, and support business outcomes
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor Degree or equivalent. Professional accounting or finance qualification and/or Master’s degree a plus.
3+ years working experience in accounting / financial services related environment.
Strong client relationship experience preferred
Progress toward or possession of a professional qualification such as CFA, CPA, or ACCA is a plus.

jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For
Responsible for planning, coordinating, analyzing, and delivering end-to-end financial reporting services for clients across APAC, EMEA, and North America. The role oversees daily service delivery, manages client relationships, and ensures reporting accuracy, quality, and compliance with established procedures. It also leads and develops a team of 6-8 professionals, working closely with global stakeholders to support strong risk management, continuous improvement, operational excellence, and business growth. Success in this role requires strong leadership, people management, communication, stakeholder management, and project management skills.
Why This Role Is Important To Us
The team you will be joining is part of State Street Global Delivery (SSGD). From core custody, accounting, fund administration, and shareholder recordkeeping to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity, and real estate, SSGD’s tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.

As
Financial Reporting, Officer,

Review, analyze, and oversee the delivery of complex periodic (quarterly, semi-annual, annual, and ad hoc) financial statements and related disclosures.
Lead team capacity planning, resource allocation, and daily operations, driving effective cross-functional collaboration to ensure efficient service delivery and business performance.

Lead people management activities, including recruitment, performance management, resource planning, and talent development, to build and maintain a high-performing, engaged team.
Manage new fund launches and client conversions, ensuring smooth implementation and operational transition. Maintain awareness of regulatory, industry, and competitor developments to support compliance, continuous improvement, and business growth.
Drive the adoption and optimization of reporting systems while identifying and implementing enhancements that improve automation, scalability, and client service delivery.
Promote a strong risk and control environment by identifying issues, monitoring compliance, and escalating breaches and operational risks in a timely manner.
Review, maintain, and enhance process documentation, including SOPs, process flows, and control frameworks, while coaching team members to follow documented processes and best practices.
Collaborate with the training liaison to design, develop, and facilitate internal training programs that support talent development and business needs.
Contribute to cross-functional projects, strategic initiatives, and administrative responsibilities as required to support wider team objectives and business priorities.
What We Value
These skills will help you succeed in this role
Strong leadership, project management, critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to analyze complex issues, assess risks and impacts, identify root causes, and deliver practical solutions in a dynamic environment.
Demonstrated people management, strategic thinking, client service, and stakeholder management capabilities, with the ability to build trusted relationships, manage expectations, influence outcomes, and collaborate effectively across global teams.
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline.
5+ years of relevant experience in financial services, including 2+ years of supervisory experience.
Postgraduate qualifications such as CFA, CPA, ACCA, or CA, whether completed or in progress, are preferred. Relevant experience in a Big 4 or reputable mid-tier accounting firm is also preferred.
Solid technical knowledge and practical experience in statutory reporting with a strong understanding of IFRS and GAAP requirements and their application.
Experience with investment funds, financial services, and investment products, with solid knowledge of applicable accounting standards.
People management experience, including recruitment, coaching, performance management, workforce planning, and talent development.
Demonstrated project management experience leading migrations or process transformation initiatives.
Experience driving process improvement, automation, and operational efficiency initiatives within a control-focused environment.
Strong analytical mindset and attention to detail, with proven ability to identify issues, develop solutions, and support informed decision-making.
Strong client service and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships, manage expectations, influence outcomes, and collaborate effectively across global teams.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including written, verbal, and listening proficiency in English.
Additional Requirements
Overtime may be required.
Ability to work across time zones when required.
Flexibility during peak reporting periods.

jobs.title: Quantitative Risk, SrAssc
jobs.descriptionText:
Who we are looking for An entry-level analyst with a strong technical and quantitative aptitude to act as a Quantitative Risk Analyst, Senior Associate based in Hangzhou, China. This role will report to the model validation lead in China, within the Model Risk Management Department Why this role is important to us Banks use models in different business functions ranging from wholesale credit, asset liability management, AML, trading, and others to risk management. Model Risk Management (MRM) involves effective challenge, which refers to the critical analysis conducted by model validator who evaluate model risk and effect appropriate changes throughout the model lifecycle, from model development to ongoing monitoring. A model validation analyst provides independent quantitative validation of models used for business and operating decisions by assessing model theoretical soundness and assumptions, evaluating data integrity, and performing sufficient quantitative testing What you will be responsible for As Quantitative Risk, Senior Associate you will
Work with team members in Hangzhou under the supervision of the model validation lead in China to support model validation activities covering models worldwide: o Support and perform independent validations on models such as credit risk, market risk, climate risk, portfolio management, pricing, and AI models by executing assigned analytical workstreams and tests. o Perform data preparation and quantitative analysis by applying statistical analysis and/or machine learning approaches to help assess whether models are performing as expected. o Assist in documenting validation work (e.g., methodology, testing approach, results, and limitations) and in compiling supporting evidence for review and reporting o Coordinate with model developers and business partners to help relay questions, issues, and feedback, and to help track actions and responses. o Contribute to streamlining the analytical process and improving pace of execution through automation and process improvements (under guidance from the validation lead). What we value These skills will help you succeed in this role
Strong analytical and quantitative mindset; ability to learn quickly and improve on existing risk methodologies and analytical approaches.
A self-assured and motivated individual able to explain analysis clearly and incorporate feedback from reviewers.
Clear and effective communication style, with an ability to adapt to various audiences without diluting effectiveness. Education & Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree (or higher) in a quantitative discipline (e.g. Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science/Engineering, or equivalents).
Prior working experience is not mandatory; internship experience, academic projects, or research experience in quantitative analytics, modeling, or risk is a plus.
Demonstrated understanding (through coursework/projects) of quantitative analytics topics relevant to credit risk and/or market risk is preferred.
Understanding in financial services regulations such as Basel, stress testing, and CCAR is a plus.
Proficient in one or more programming languages such as Python, R, or Matlab. Additional requirements
Ability to take initiative, manage assigned tasks, and meet deadlines in a team-based environment.
Finance and/or risk management certificates like CFA and FRM are a plus but not required.

This opportunity is ideal for individuals interested in contributing to our team as an Application Developer Intern within State Street’s Global Technology Services organization. Our technology function, Global Technology Services (GTS), is vital to State Street and is the key enabler for our business to deliver data and insights to our clients. What You Will Do:
In this role, you will perform the following day-to-day activities:
Design and develop IS Tech APAC applications that support various business requirement from investment services APAC. It will follow standard software development lifecycle like Agile, Kanban or etc. The coding language will be Java as primary.
Build and manage databases using a combination of database technologies
Create responsive user interfaces with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and frameworks like React or Angular
Write unit and integration tests
Participate in design and code reviews
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to manage dependencies, identify risks, and deliver solutions
In This Role, You Will Have
Engagement in meaningful daily work: You'll take ownership of specific tasks and projects, gaining hands-on experience and building confidence through real contributions.
A supportive learning environment: You'll exercise your judgment in a guided setting, with mentorship and supervision to help you grow.
Focused skill development: This role is designed to help you deepen your expertise in a specific area.
Clear structure and expectations: You'll work within well-defined parameters, giving you the clarity and focus to succeed.
Independent contributions: You'll have the opportunity to make an impact through your individual contributions while collaborating with a supportive team.
Focus on growth: While there are no people management responsibilities with this role, it is a great stepping stone for future leadership opportunities.
A collaborative team culture: You'll build strong working relationships with your peers and supervisor, gaining valuable experience in a professional environment.
Education And Preferred Qualifications
Candidates should be:
Final-year undergraduate or graduate students pursuing degrees in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related technical disciplines who are interested in converting to a full-time role post-graduation
Enthusiastic about building a long-term career in a dynamic, technology-driven organization
Effective communicators with the ability to collaborate in a team-oriented environment
Open to feedback and committed to continuous learning and improvement
Motivated by real-world problem solving and eager to contribute innovative ideas
Certification Nice To Haves
AWS/Azure Certified Developer
AWS/Azure SysOps Administrator or equivalent
B.S. Computer Science/Engineering or related fields

Candidates should exhibit working knowledge of the following key skills and proficiencies:

Cloud Computing
Java
Communication

Python
GenAI related knowledge

jobs.descriptionText:
Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for a
motivated Software Engineering Intern
to join our Transaction Services Platforms team. The internship offers hands-on exposure to Java-based transaction applications. These mission-critical platforms support Middle Office and Back Office functions by processing, validating, enriching, storing, and reconciling transaction and reference data across multiple systems.
The role is ideal for a
current university student
who is passionate about technology, eager to learn Java and software engineering skills, and keen to gain real-world experience in large-scale transaction processing solutions.
No prior professional experience is required
; you will work under the guidance of a mentor and experienced team members.
Learn and contribute to Java solutions for transaction processing and reconciliation
Experience the software development lifecycle, from requirements and development through testing, deployment, and monitoring
Learn TDD, CI/CD, automation, and engineering best practices with close guidance from a mentor
What You Will
Do
Learning & Development Tasks
Learn about the Transaction Services business and platforms by working with business analysts, product owners, and engineering teams.
Assist in developing and enhancing Java services for small features and platform improvements under supervision.
Write clean, maintainable, and testable Java and SQL code in line with team standards and mentor feedback.
Help analyze data, logs, and test results to support testing, troubleshooting, and solution validation.
Observe and participate in team discussions, code reviews, and design sessions to build technical understanding.
Execution, Quality & Support
Learn and apply TDD, CI/CD, and automated testing in day-to-day work.
Assist with system testing, UAT, and issue investigation under the guidance of senior engineers.
Gain exposure to high-volume, time-sensitive transaction processing, with attention to accuracy and quality.
Follow established controls and engineering practices that protect system stability, data integrity, and operational resilience.
Collaboration & Growth
Provide regular updates on progress, questions, and blockers to your mentor and the team.
Collaborate with global, cross-functional teams and learn how they work together.
Take ownership of assigned tasks and ask for help early when needed.
Complete a small project or deliverable during the internship and share learnings with the team.
What We Value
Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail.
A curious, proactive learner who communicates clearly and welcomes feedback.
A quality-focused mindset with accountability for assigned work.
A willingness to learn how an Agile/Scrum environment works.
The ability to manage time and deliver tasks within agreed timelines.
Education & Qualifications/Skills
Basic Qualifications
Currently pursuing a university degree, with no professional experience required.
Foundational knowledge of Java and object-oriented programming through coursework or personal projects.
Basic understanding of SQL and relational databases.
Basic understanding of data structures, algorithms, and software design principles.
Strong interest in learning modern engineering practices, such as unit testing, CI/CD, and Agile development.
Preferred Qualifications
Familiarity with Spring or Spring Boot.
Exposure to messaging and streaming technologies such as MQ or Kafka.
Familiarity with Git, cloud platforms (such as AWS or Azure), or container technologies such as Docker.
Relevant coursework, personal projects, hackathons, or prior internships in software engineering.
Interest in financial services and transaction processing.
Education
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree program in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline.
Good oral and written English communication skills.
Where the Role Will Be Based
The role will be based in Hangzhou, China.

.

Generate effective status and progress reports to the QA Manager and project team members.

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer - ADR
jobs.descriptionText:
Who We’re Looking For
The State Street Cyber Security Architecture & Engineering team is seeking an accomplished professional with proven expertise in Application Security (AppSec), Application Detection and Response (ADR), and DevSecOps. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience in application security, threat detection, incident response, secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC), and the implementation of runtime application protection and monitoring technologies.
The successful candidate will be responsible for designing, implementing, and supporting ADR capabilities that provide visibility into application-layer threats, attacks, and vulnerabilities across our enterprise application portfolio. This role requires strong technical expertise, a security-first mindset, and a passion for partnering with development, engineering, and cybersecurity teams to enhance application security posture and detection capabilities.
What You Will Be Responsible For
Help define and build the organization's Application Detection and Response (ADR) strategy, integrating runtime application security monitoring and threat detection into the broader Application Security and DevSecOps programs.
Partner with Engineering, Security Operations, Cloud Security, and Application Development teams to implement and operationalize ADR technologies and processes.
Lead the deployment, onboarding, and operational support of ADR platforms, ensuring effective integration with enterprise applications and security tooling.
Monitor, analyze, and investigate application-layer security events, attack patterns, and anomalous behaviors identified through ADR solutions.
Collaborate with application teams to triage, prioritize, and remediate security findings, threats, and attack indicators detected within applications.
Develop use cases, detection logic, alerting mechanisms, and response workflows to improve visibility into application threats and reduce response times.
Integrate ADR platforms with incident response processes.
Deliver and communicate security reporting, dashboards, metrics, and executive-level summaries related to application threats, attacks, and remediation activities.
Develop and maintain ADR, AppSec, and DevSecOps documentation, standards, and operational procedures.
Support internal and external audits by providing evidence, documentation, and process adherence related to application security monitoring and response capabilities.
Work with stakeholders to continuously improve application monitoring, detection accuracy, response effectiveness, and security processes.
Provide technical leadership and support for strategic projects through planning, implementation, and operationalization.
What We Value
These skills will help you succeed in this role
Strong software development background with technologies such as Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, or similar platforms.
Experience with cloud technologies including Azure and AWS.
Experience in Application Security disciplines, including SAST, DAST, SCA, API Security, Container Security, and Secure SDLC practices.
Experience implementing or supporting Application Detection and Response (ADR), Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), Web Application and API Protection (WAAP), API Security, Threat Detection, or related application security technologies.
Strong understanding of attack techniques targeting web, mobile, cloud-native, and API-based applications, including OWASP Top 10, API security risks, and advanced threat scenarios.
Experience analyzing application telemetry, logs, traces, and security events to identify malicious activity and investigate incidents.
Current information security certifications such as CISSP, GCIH, GWAPT, or equivalent is highly desirable.
Experience with automation and orchestration technologies such as Ansible, Terraform, Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) practices.
Proven technical solutioning experience with current and emerging technologies including Agile Development, DevOps, Cloud Engineering, Cloud Security, Application Security, Threat Detection, Incident Response, and Cybersecurity.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across technical, operational, and executive audiences.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple initiatives, operational responsibilities, incidents, and projects simultaneously.
Education & Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in information technology (IT), computer science, or related field with 6 years of relevant experience.
Experience in software development and secure software development lifecycle (SDLC).
Experience with application security tooling and its operations with modern CI/CD, and DevSecOps best practices.
Experience partnering with Dev community to influence without authority to adopt application security best practices, and tooling.
Security+ or other cybersecurity security certification.
Experience with Agile and scrum practices.
Salary Range
$120,000 - $202,500 Annual
The range quoted above applies to the role in the primary location specified. If the candidate would ultimately work outside of the primary location above, the applicable range could differ.
Employees are eligible to participate in State Street’s comprehensive benefits program, which includes: our retirement savings plan (401K) with company match; insurance coverage including basic life, medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and other optional additional coverages; paid-time off including vacation, sick leave, short term disability, and family care responsibilities; access to our Employee Assistance Program; incentive compensation including eligibility for annual performance-based awards (excluding certain sales roles subject to sales incentive plans); and, eligibility for certain tax advantaged savings plans.
For a full overview, visit
https://hrportal.ehr.com/statestreet/Home
.
